q: Which statement best describes the approach of SQMS No. 1, A Firm's System of Quality Management?
choices: Firms adopt a standard set of quality control policies listed in the standard
Firms establish quality objectives, identify and assess quality risks, and design and implement responses to those risks
Firms rely on peer review to design their quality policies
Quality management applies only to firms that audit public companies
exp: SQMS 1 uses a risk-based approach in which the firm sets quality objectives, identifies and assesses quality risks to achieving them, and designs and implements responses tailored to the firm. It replaced the more prescriptive policy-based quality control standards and applies to all firms performing engagements under AICPA standards.

q: Which of the following is one of the eight components of a system of quality management under SQMS 1?
choices: Peer review
Client profitability analysis
The firm's risk assessment process
Engagement budgeting
exp: The eight components are governance and leadership, the firm's risk assessment process, relevant ethical requirements, acceptance and continuance, engagement performance, resources, information and communication, and the monitoring and remediation process. Peer review is an external program, not a component.

q: Under SQMS 1, who should be assigned ultimate responsibility and accountability for the firm's system of quality management?
choices: The firm's chief executive officer or managing partner, or the managing board of partners
The partner in charge of the largest engagement
The firm's peer reviewer
Each engagement partner, for their own engagements
exp: SQMS 1 requires the firm to assign ultimate responsibility and accountability for the system to its CEO or managing partner (or equivalent), with operational responsibility assigned to others as appropriate. Engagement partners are responsible for quality on their engagements, not for the firm-wide system.

q: How often must the individual with ultimate responsibility evaluate the firm's system of quality management under SQMS 1?
choices: Every three years, aligned with peer review
Only when a deficiency is identified
Monthly
At least annually, concluding whether the system provides reasonable assurance that its quality objectives are being achieved
exp: SQMS 1 requires an evaluation of the system at least annually, concluding whether it provides reasonable assurance that the firm's quality objectives are achieved. The peer review cycle is a separate external process.

q: A firm's monitoring identifies that several engagement teams failed to document their evaluation of accounting estimates. What does SQMS 1 require the firm to do next?
choices: Report the matter to the AICPA
Investigate the root cause of the deficiency and design remedial actions that respond to it
Reissue the affected audit reports
Dismiss the engagement partners involved
exp: SQMS 1 requires the firm to evaluate identified findings to determine whether deficiencies exist, investigate their root causes, and design and implement remedial actions responsive to those causes. Reissuing reports or dismissing staff are not required responses.

q: Under SQMS 1, for which engagements must the firm require an engagement quality review?
choices: All audits of financial statements
Only engagements for public companies
Engagements for which an engagement quality review is required by law or regulation, and engagements for which the firm determines it is an appropriate response to quality risks
Engagements with fees above a set threshold
exp: SQMS 1 requires an engagement quality review when required by law or regulation and when the firm determines that it is an appropriate response to assessed quality risks, based on its own criteria. It is not required for every audit, and fees alone are not the criterion.

q: A firm uses audit software and methodology provided by its international network. Under SQMS 1, who is responsible for the firm's system of quality management?
choices: The firm remains responsible and should evaluate how network requirements and services affect its system
The network, because it supplies the methodology
The software vendor
Responsibility is shared equally between the firm and the network
exp: SQMS 1 makes the firm responsible for its own system, so it must understand network requirements and services, determine how they affect the system, and evaluate whether they need to be adapted or supplemented. Using network resources does not transfer responsibility.

q: Which individual would be ineligible to serve as engagement quality reviewer on an audit under SQMS 2?
choices: A partner in another office of the firm with relevant industry experience
An individual from outside the firm with appropriate competence and authority
A senior manager with sufficient technical expertise and authority
A manager who is a member of the engagement team for that audit
exp: The engagement quality reviewer cannot be a member of the engagement team, because objectivity is essential to evaluating the team's judgments. SQMS 2 permits individuals from outside the firm or other offices who have the necessary competence, capabilities, time and authority.

q: Under SQMS 2, why does a firm need policies addressing whether a former engagement partner may become the engagement quality reviewer on the same engagement?
choices: To ensure the reviewer has enough time
Because previous involvement as engagement partner threatens the reviewer's objectivity, so a cooling-off period is needed
Because former engagement partners lack competence
To comply with peer review rules on fees
exp: SQMS 2 requires policies limiting the eligibility of an individual to become engagement quality reviewer on an engagement where the individual previously served as engagement partner, which addresses the threat that they would be reviewing their own past judgments. Competence and time are separate eligibility criteria.

q: What is the primary focus of an engagement quality review under SQMS 2?
choices: Reperforming the engagement team's tests of details
Approving the engagement budget
Objectively evaluating the significant judgments made by the engagement team and the conclusions reached
Confirming account balances with third parties
exp: The engagement quality review is an objective evaluation of the significant judgments made and conclusions reached by the engagement team, performed at appropriate points during the engagement. It is not a reperformance of the audit.

q: An audit is subject to an engagement quality review. When may the engagement partner date the auditor's report?
choices: Only after being notified that the engagement quality review is complete
Before the review, as long as the reviewer completes it within 60 days
At any time, because the review is optional
Only after the client approves the reviewer's comments
exp: AU-C 220 and SQMS 2 prohibit the engagement partner from dating the report until notified by the engagement quality reviewer that the review is complete. The review is a precondition to dating the report, not a post-issuance step.

q: Under AU-C 220 as revised by SAS 146, which statement about the engagement partner's responsibility is correct?
choices: The engagement partner may delegate overall responsibility for quality to the engagement manager
The engagement partner is responsible only for reviewing the final report
The engagement quality reviewer shares responsibility for the opinion
The engagement partner has overall responsibility for managing and achieving quality on the engagement and must be sufficiently and appropriately involved throughout
exp: SAS 146 places overall responsibility for managing and achieving quality on the engagement partner, who must be sufficiently and appropriately involved throughout the engagement. The partner may assign procedures and tasks to others but cannot delegate that overall responsibility.

q: During an audit, the engagement partner and a member of the firm's technical group disagree about the accounting for a complex transaction. Under AU-C 220, what must happen before the report is dated?
choices: The engagement partner's view prevails automatically
The difference of opinion must be resolved in accordance with the firm's policies
The matter must be referred to the client's audit committee for resolution
The disagreement must be disclosed in the auditor's report
exp: AU-C 220 requires differences of opinion within the engagement team, or with consultants or the engagement quality reviewer, to be dealt with and resolved under the firm's policies before the report is dated. The client has no role in resolving internal firm disagreements.

q: Which action by an engagement partner best demonstrates compliance with AU-C 220 requirements for resources?
choices: Assigning staff based solely on availability
Assuming all staff assigned by the scheduling department are qualified
Letting the client choose engagement team members
Determining that team members collectively have the appropriate competence, capabilities and time to perform the engagement
exp: The engagement partner must determine that sufficient and appropriate resources are assigned or made available in a timely manner, including team members with the needed competence, capabilities and time. Relying solely on availability or scheduling does not meet that responsibility.

q: An audit report was released to the client on April 5. Under AU-C 230, what is the latest documentation completion date?
choices: May 5
May 20
June 4
July 5
exp: The final audit file must be assembled no later than 60 days after the report release date: April 5 + 25 days = April 30, + 31 = May 31, + 4 = June 4. May 20 is only 45 days after release, and July 5 is three months after release.

q: An auditor released the report for a nonissuer client on April 5, 2026. Under AICPA standards, until what date at a minimum must the audit documentation be retained?
choices: April 5, 2031
April 5, 2033
June 4, 2031
December 31, 2031
exp: AU-C 230 requires retention for no shorter than five years from the report release date, so April 5, 2026 + 5 years = April 5, 2031. Seven years applies to audits under PCAOB standards.

q: After the documentation completion date, an auditor realizes a workpaper is incomplete and wants to add an explanation. What does AU-C 230 require?
choices: Replace the original workpaper with a corrected version
Delete the incomplete workpaper
No changes are allowed after the completion date
Do not delete or discard documentation, and document the additions, including when and by whom they were made, the reasons, and their effect on conclusions
exp: After the documentation completion date, the auditor must not delete or discard documentation, but may add to it if the additions are documented with when and by whom they were made, the reasons and their effect on conclusions. Replacing the original would destroy existing documentation.

q: Between the report release date and the documentation completion date, which change to audit documentation is appropriate?
choices: Performing new audit procedures to support the opinion
Deleting superseded documentation, sorting and cross-referencing workpapers, and signing off on completion checklists
Changing the conclusions reached on significant matters
Removing evidence that conflicts with the final conclusion
exp: Assembly of the final file is an administrative process, such as discarding superseded drafts, sorting, cross-referencing and completing checklists, and does not involve new procedures or new conclusions. Removing contradictory evidence is never appropriate.

q: Under AU-C 230, what standard should audit documentation meet?
choices: It should enable an experienced auditor with no previous connection to the audit to understand the procedures performed, the evidence obtained and the significant findings and conclusions
It should be understandable to the client's board without explanation
It should include every matter the auditor considered
It should contain copies of all of the client's accounting records
exp: The experienced auditor standard requires documentation sufficient for an experienced auditor with no connection to the engagement to understand the nature, timing and extent of procedures, the results and evidence, and significant findings and conclusions. Documenting every matter considered or copying all client records is not required.

q: In documenting a test of details, what does AU-C 230 require the auditor to record about the items tested?
choices: Only the total dollar amount tested
The names of the client employees who prepared each document
The identifying characteristics of the specific items or matters tested
A photocopy of every document examined
exp: Recording identifying characteristics, such as invoice numbers or selection criteria, allows the work to be understood and reviewed. Photocopies of every document are not required, and a total amount alone does not identify what was tested.

q: Which information must be documented for each piece of audit work?
choices: Only who performed the work
The hours spent and the billing rate
The client's approval of the work
Who performed the work and the date completed, and who reviewed it and the date and extent of the review
exp: AU-C 230 requires documentation of who performed the work and when, and who reviewed it, with the date and extent of review. Hours, billing rates and client approval are not documentation requirements.

q: In exceptional circumstances, an auditor judges it necessary to depart from a presumptively mandatory requirement in GAAS. What must the auditor document?
choices: The justification for the departure and how the alternative procedures performed were sufficient to achieve the requirement's objective
Nothing, because presumptively mandatory requirements are optional
The client's approval of the departure
A statement in the audit report explaining the departure
exp: When the auditor departs from a presumptively mandatory requirement, AU-C 230 requires documentation of the justification and how alternative procedures achieved the objective of the requirement. Such departures are rare and do not require client approval or disclosure in the report.

q: An auditor identified information that was inconsistent with the auditor's final conclusion about a significant matter. What does AU-C 230 require?
choices: Remove the inconsistent information from the file
Document how the auditor addressed the inconsistency
Disclose the inconsistency in the audit report
Obtain management's representation that the information is wrong
exp: AU-C 230 requires the auditor to document how the inconsistency with the final conclusion was addressed. Removing contrary evidence would misrepresent the basis for the conclusion.

q: Which statement about oral explanations as audit documentation is correct?
choices: Oral explanations are sufficient to support the auditor's work
Oral explanations may never be used in any way
Oral explanations alone do not adequately support the work or conclusions, but may clarify information in the documentation
Oral explanations are acceptable if provided by the engagement partner
exp: Oral explanations alone are not adequate support for the work performed or conclusions reached, though they may explain or clarify information that is documented. Even the engagement partner's explanations must be supported by written documentation.

q: What is the earliest date an auditor may date the auditor's report?
choices: The date the financial statements are issued
The balance sheet date
The date the engagement letter was signed
The date the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, including evidence that the audit documentation has been reviewed
exp: AU-C 700 requires the report to be dated no earlier than when sufficient appropriate evidence has been obtained, including evidence that documentation has been reviewed and the statements, with disclosures, have been prepared and management has taken responsibility. The report release date is usually later.

q: After releasing the report, the auditor performs new procedures because of facts discovered later. What does AU-C 230 require the auditor to document?
choices: Nothing, because the documentation completion date has passed
The circumstances, the new or additional procedures performed, evidence obtained and conclusions reached, and who made and reviewed the changes
Only the revised opinion
Only the date the facts were discovered
exp: When the auditor performs new or additional procedures or reaches new conclusions after the report date, AU-C 230 requires documentation of the circumstances, the procedures, evidence and conclusions, and who made and reviewed the changes. Documentation is required even after the completion date.

q: A client asks for copies of all audit documentation for its records. Which statement is correct?
choices: Audit documentation is the property of the auditor, and while portions may be shared with the client, it is not a substitute for the client's accounting records
Audit documentation belongs to the client and must be provided on request
Audit documentation belongs to the client's board
Audit documentation must be destroyed once the report is released
exp: Audit documentation is the auditor's property, and the auditor may make portions available to the client at its discretion, provided this does not undermine the audit. It is not a substitute for the client's records and must be retained for the required period.

q: Under AU-C 230, which item is the auditor generally not required to keep in the final audit file?
choices: Documentation of significant findings and discussions with management
Evidence of who reviewed key workpapers
Superseded drafts of workpapers and financial statements
Documentation of how inconsistencies with final conclusions were resolved
exp: Superseded drafts, notes reflecting incomplete thinking and duplicates generally need not be retained. Significant findings, review evidence and the resolution of inconsistencies must be documented.

q: In assessing a firm's acceptance and continuance responses under SQMS 1, which consideration is most directly relevant?
choices: The client's preferred engagement partner
Whether the firm has the resources and competence to perform the engagement and information about the integrity and ethical values of the client
The size of the expected fee compared with the firm's other clients
Whether the client has previously been audited
exp: SQMS 1 requires judgments about accepting or continuing engagements to consider the nature and circumstances of the engagement, the integrity and ethical values of the client, and whether the firm can perform it with the required resources and competence. Fees should not override those judgments.

q: An auditor discusses a significant accounting issue with the client's CFO. Which documentation is required by AU-C 230?
choices: A recording of the meeting
Nothing, if the issue was resolved
The CFO's signed agreement with the auditor's view
The significant matter discussed, when and with whom it was discussed
exp: AU-C 230 requires documentation of discussions of significant findings or issues with management, those charged with governance and others, including the nature of the matters and when and with whom the discussions took place. Resolution does not eliminate the need to document.
